meta.title: Two-port parameters: Z, Y and S matrices
meta.tools: Two-port extraction by AC simulation (test sources at each port), Z↔Y↔S conversions, reciprocity and losslessness checks
meta.summary: Extract the Z and Y matrices of a π-network and an LC filter by simulating test excitations, convert them to scattering parameters, and verify the identities that must hold: Y = Z⁻¹, reciprocity (S₁₂ = S₂₁) and, for lossless networks, SᴴS = I.
meta.problem: A two-port is fully described by a 2×2 matrix — but which one, and how do they relate?
meta.theory:
Z: v = Zi (open-circuit tests), Y = Z⁻¹ (short-circuit tests). With reference impedance Z0: $S=(Z-Z_0I)(Z+Z_0I)^{-1}$ (normalised). Reciprocal (passive, no ferrites) networks have Z₁₂ = Z₂₁ ⇒ S₁₂ = S₂₁;
lossless networks have unitary S: $|S_{11}|^2+|S_{21}|^2=1$ at every frequency. For a symmetric π-network the analytic Y is $[[Y_a+Y_c, -Y_c], [-Y_c, Y_b+Y_c]]$.
meta.method:
π-network: shunt 100 Ω, series 50 Ω + 1 µH, shunt 200 Ω || 1 nF, at 1–100 MHz. LC: 3rd-order Butterworth low-pass (50 Ω, 30 MHz), lossless. Z from two open-circuit simulations (1 A into each port),
Y from two short-circuit simulations (1 V at each port); S from Z.
meta.track: Applied Mathematics — 218 projects in electrical engineering
